text:
Maya: Morning — quick async update from model onboarding: pushed goliath-smallq@v1.3 to staging. Ran our standard evals against the 'support-short' promptset and saw a quality drop (~4.2% relative). Leaving notes and next steps here.

Jae: Can you paste the eval summary and any failing prompts?

Maya: Sure — brief summary below (samples truncated).
```
model: goliath-smallq@v1.3
promptset: support-short
samples: 200
metric: answer_quality (normalized) 86.4% (baseline v1.2: 90.6%)
avg_latency: 42ms
regressions: 9 flagged (hallucination ↑, truncation on long ctx)
notes: quantization profile changed (int8 fast-path); kernel switch attempted
```

Ravi: Sounds like either quantization or a KV cache warming issue — both can cause truncation and hallucination patterns. Did the onboard script change qconfig?

Maya: I only updated the conversion pipeline to use the new fast int8 recipe (to reduce cost). Conversion diff: kept attention dims, changed weight packing. No KV code touched in the model package, but runtime kernel selection moved from xformers->custom for that layer.

Lina: I spotted 2 failing prompts that are long (context ~2.5k tokens) — output gets cut off around where prefix cache should have been warmed. Could be batch/window heuristic.

ops-bot: deploy status: staging deploy goliath-smallq@v1.3 — build #4578 — succeeded :white_check_mark:

Jae: @Maya can you add the failing prompts to the regression harness and open a gate PR? If regressions > 5 we hold rollout and run comparisons.

Maya: Yep. Created PR 4523 to add 9 failing prompts to gating set and added a smoke job. Also attached raw outputs and a minimal repro. Repro snippet below: 
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"goliath-smallq@v1.3","prompt":"<long support convo...>","max_tokens":256}' \
  https://staging-api.redwood-inference.test/v1/generate | jq .
```

Ravi: I'll look at kernel selection and quantization profile. If we roll back the fast-path quant, we can re-run evals to isolate. Also please include the conversion logs (quant table) in the PR.

Lina: For rollout policy — current plan was 25% canary -> 100%. My suggestion: hold canary, run targeted experiments: 1) v1.3 with quant disabled, 2) v1.3 with original kernel, 3) v1.2 baseline. If any of those fixes regressions, we pick that mitigation and re-run gating.

Maya: Agree. I'm rolling canary back to 0% now and kicking off 3 eval jobs. Plan today: 1) reproduce locally + capture logs (ETA 2–3h), 2) add failing prompts to the gating suite (PR 4523), 3) try conversion with quant disabled and run metric diff, 4) ping for quick PR review.

Jae: ETA for review on 4523? I can take it if you're swamped.

Maya: Thanks — I added a short checklist in the PR description. Would love a quick glance from @Ravi for conversion logs and @Lina for gating semantics. If either of you can review in the next 30–45m that helps.

Ravi: I can review in ~30m. I'll look for conversion logs and the quant table. Also check the kernel switch traces — sometimes the new kernel uses a different attention math (approx) that changes outputs.

Lina: I'll review gating + update modelcard to note short-long-context caveat if we find it's a known tradeoff.

Maya: Small note — one of the flagged prompts is a legal-style answer where hallucination risk is high; we should probably tighten post-processing for that class even if backend fix is found. Adding a category tag in the PR.

ops-bot: reminder: scheduled maintenance window at 2026-03-19T03:00Z — no impact expected to staging.

Jae: Cool. Keep us posted in this thread. If you can't repro in 3 hours, shout and we'll pair.

Maya: Will update. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
